b. Soils and Geology
(1) Geology
The impact of the proposed project on the geology of the area will be miniscule since very little subsurface activity will occur.
The quality and load bearing capacity of the projects underlying geologic structure, rock mantles and bedrock may have some impact on the development of the projected multi-family apartment construction in the Front Street area. The possible impact, in this regard, cannot be assessed without detailed investigations of specific site locations. A program of subsurface exploration, including test borings, under the supervision of an engineering geologist or construction engineer will be needed to determine the feasibility of the sites for the type of new construction projected for them.
(2) Soils
Soils, likewise, will be affected only to a minor degree by the proposed project. Project soils have already lost their profiles by the degree of urbanization that has already occurred in the area. The productive capacity of the soils is not on issue due to the present land use. However, it should be noted that there are no known polluting agents that will be produced by the proposed project to further diminish soil productivity. In some areas, parks, open spaces and landscaped areas, the quality of the soil will be improved by the addition of top soil fill.
The only impact to project soils that could be imagined, is that of erosion of the clean sites. Minor erosion may also occur at building sites during the construction periods. The improbable situation of heavy erosion in the project area is not likely due to the low relief of the area.
To further prevent the likelihood of erosion, cleared areas will be planted with grass as part of the project activity during the execution stages of the project.
Soil load bearing capacity could have an impact (possibly minor negative) on new construction of multistory structures in the area; however, as in the discussion of geologic characteristics above, individual site testing would be required to determine this. Test borings are not a part of the planned project activity.
